turns.text: There are no competitors. Nobody makes flashcards from slides with AI.
turns.reply:
"Nobody does this" is almost never true, and it's the riskiest claim to leave untested. Anki, Quizlet, Notion AI, and even ChatGPT let students paste slide text and generate cards today — the question is what FlashForge does that those tools don't, and why a student would switch.

This matters because if a free or cheap alternative already exists, your value proposition needs to be sharper than "AI flashcards from slides."

This week, Leo: open ChatGPT or Quizlet's AI feature, upload a real lecture slide deck, and generate a set of flashcards. Note exactly where it falls short — that gap is your real value proposition.

What does FlashForge do that a student can't get by dropping their PDF into ChatGPT right now?
updates: New assumption H1: No meaningful competitor makes AI-generated flashcards from lecture slides.

turns.text: Quizlet does flashcards, but ours is better because it uses AI.
turns.reply:
Quizlet has had AI-generated flashcards since 2023, so "we use AI" isn't a differentiator — it's a feature they already have. The real question is *how* FlashForge is better in a way a student would notice and pay for.

That gap is your moat: if you can't name it precisely, a student will just use the free tool they already have.

You have an open task to test this yourself — upload a real slide deck to Quizlet AI and ChatGPT, generate cards, and write down the three specific things that frustrate you. That friction is your starting point.

What specifically breaks down when a student uses Quizlet AI on a lecture slide deck — formatting, accuracy, slide structure, something else?
